title: cwc-continental-1998-southern-states-heavyweight
label: Eric Smart

won.source: Received the belt directly from Tommy Lane as the title moved to the Georgia region, per the council's own commissioner.

note: No further Southern States Heavyweight title document survives in the held record.

title: cwc-continental-1998-southern-states-heavyweight
label: Tommy Lane

won.source: Billed as Southern States Heavyweight Champion in the council's own 25 January 1998 rankings bulletin; no earlier title-change document survives.

lost.source: Handed the belt directly to Eric Smart on-air as the title moved from the Southern region to the Georgia region, per the council's own commissioner.

note: Transferred, not lost in a match, as part of the council's own regional restructuring at Southern Justice.

title: cwc-continental-1998-southern-states-tag-team
label: Thunderstorm

won.source: Received the belts directly from the Electric Mayhem as the title moved to the Georgia region; the broadcast's own text names only a single recipient for the paired belts.

lost.source: Declared vacant on the spot by the Georgia region's own official for want of any ranked contenders.

note: Recorded exactly as the council's own broadcast narrated it, including naming one man for a tag title.

title: cwc-continental-1998-southern-states-tag-team
label: The Polo Club

won.source: Billed as Southern States Tag Team Champions in the council's own 25 January 1998 rankings bulletin; no earlier title-change document survives.

lost.source: Handed the belts directly to Thunderstorm on-air as the title moved from the Southern region to the Georgia region, per the council's own commissioner.

note: Transferred, not lost in a match, as part of the council's own regional restructuring at Southern Justice.

title: cwc-continental-1998-southern-states-tag-team
label: The Hot House

won.source: Billed as Southern States Tag Team Champions, defending the title in the Georgia region's own In Memory of the Fallen supercard of 31 May 1998; no document bridges the vacancy declared at Southern Justice to this reign.

note: Retained against the New British Lions by double countout on 31 May 1998.

title: cwc-continental-1998-tennessee
label: Carolina Crusher

won.source: Billed as Tennessee Champion in the council's own 25 January 1998 rankings bulletin; no title-change document survives.

note: Ambushed by the returning "Roadkill" Len Griffin, who demanded a title shot; no further document survives recording the outcome.

won.source: Installed as the first Mid-South Heavyweight Champion by the region's own commissioner, Kay, immediately after giving up the Southern States Heavyweight Championship.
Installed as the first Mid-South Tag Team Champions by the region's own commissioner, Kay, immediately after giving up the Southern States Tag Team Championship.

title: cwc-continental-1998-mid-atlantic-heavyweight
label: "The Crippler" Rex Stone

won.source: Won a six-man battle royal for the vacant Mid-Atlantic Heavyweight Championship, last eliminating "Iceman" David Smith, per the region's own 31 January 1998 broadcast.

note: The title was billed vacant beforehand; no prior champion is recorded in the held record.

won.source: Billed as Mid-Atlantic Tag Team Champions in the council's own 25 January 1998 rankings bulletin; no title-change document survives.

title: cwc-continental-1998-florida-heavyweight
label: Richard Richardson

won.source: Billed as Florida Heavyweight Champion in the council's own 25 January 1998 rankings bulletin; no earlier title-change document survives.

note: Retained against a masked "Grave Robber #1" stand-in after the crowd was led to expect a Hangman title challenge.

won.source: Won the Georgia State Championship from Logan Gunz with the "Mob Hit" frog splash after both men crashed through the timekeeper's table.

title: cwc-continental-1998-georgia-state
label: Logan Gunz

won.source: Billed as reigning Georgia State Champion at the start of the Georgia region's own In Memory of the Fallen supercard, 31 May 1998; no earlier title-change document survives.

lost.source: Pinned by Jimmy "Pretty Boy" Floyd's top-rope frog splash, "Mob Hit," after both men crashed through the timekeeper's table.

how: Pinned following the "Mob Hit" frog splash.

title: cwc-continental-1998-georgia-state-tag-team
label: "Big Daddy" Jason Wallace & "Bad News" Ben Mullins

won.source: Won the vacant Georgia State Tag Team Championship tournament final over the U.S. Bulldogs after Ian Walker maced John Weyrauch.

note: The title was contested as a vacant tournament final; no prior champions are recorded in the held record.

title: cwc-continental-1998-atlanta-city
label: Aaron D'Arby

won.source: Billed as reigning Atlanta City Champion at the start of the Georgia region's own In Memory of the Fallen supercard, 31 May 1998; no earlier title-change document survives.

note: Retained against Neil Finan; B-Onez earned a future title shot by winning the same card's fifteen-man battle royal.
